Description Hello Valve Development Team, I would like to report a possible issue with Dota 2's reporting and Behavior Score system. My Behavior Score recently dropped from 5,926 to 5,461, a loss of 465 points, and I received a temporary matchmaking restriction of approximately four hours. My latest Conduct Summary Matches evaluated: 15 Positive matches: 12 Reported matches: 3 Reports: 9 Reporting parties: 9 Communication reports: 0 Abandoned matches: 0 Commends: 21 Excessive Reports: Yes Description of the problem My account currently has communication restrictions due to its Behavior Score, meaning I cannot use text or voice chat. When teammates become toxic, I mute them, report inappropriate behavior when necessary, and continue playing normally. I use map pings to communicate gameplay information. Sometimes teammates repeatedly demand that I join fights that I believe are strategically unfavorable. When I choose not to participate in those fights to avoid unnecessary deaths, I suspect some teammates retaliate by reporting me. I understand that refusing a teammate's call does not automatically prove that their report is abusive. However, I am concerned that the reporting system may be penalizing legitimate strategic disagreements. Expected behavior Reports should be evaluated based on actual disruptive gameplay rather than simply disagreement between teammates. Actual behavior My account received nine reports across three reported matches, followed by a significant Behavior Score reduction and an approximately four-hour matchmaking restriction. I cannot confirm that these reports directly caused the restriction, but the timing raises concerns. Request Could the development team investigate whether the reporting system is correctly handling potentially retaliatory reports? If a system error is identified, I respectfully request that the resulting Behavior Score reduction and matchmaking restriction be reviewed and corrected where possible. Thank you for your time and consideration. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No Description Hello Valve developers, I would like to report a possible issue with the Behavior Score and Overwatch systems in Dota 2. On October 14, 2026, I received a 24-hour matchmaking ban with a notification stating that Overwatch had found me guilty of a gameplay violation. At the same time, my Behavior Score dropped from 2,215 to 1,465. However, my latest conduct summary shows the following statistics: - 15 matches played - 14 positive matches - Only 1 report - 39 commends - 0 abandoned matches - 0 communication reports - Excessive Reports: Yes I find this particularly confusing because the system marked my account as having excessive reports despite showing only one report in the latest summary. Recently, I have been playing Turbo matches to practice Invoker. I deliberately chose Turbo because I am still learning the hero and do not want to negatively affect other players in ranked or regular All Pick matches. I have not intentionally fed, griefed, or attempted to ruin anyone's games. I have simply been practicing a difficult hero while trying my best to win. I understand that making mistakes while learning a hero is normal, but I do not believe that poor performance alone should be treated as intentional griefing. I kindly ask the developers to investigate the following: 1. Why did my Behavior Score decrease despite having only one report and 39 commends? 2. Why was my account flagged with "Excessive Reports: Yes"? 3. Was the Overwatch punishment correctly applied? 4. Is there a possible issue affecting players with already low Behavior Scores? If this punishment was issued incorrectly, I would appreciate a review and restoration of the Behavior Score points that were unfairly deducted. I have attached a screenshot of my conduct summary as supporting evidence. Thank you for your time and attention. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 9044490273 ### Screenshots _No Description Good afternoon. I feel like the politeness system in Dota undermines the team aspect of the game, because in a game where you need to coordinate and work together to find ways to win, people can’t speak in voice chat or even type a message in the chat. Before, if you didn’t like someone, you could just mute them in-game and keep playing, but now even good players have to play without a microphone and often lose games because of it. Solving this problem would also address the issue of multi-accounting, since people most often create new accounts because of communication score. Also, sometimes when you write in-game chat messages, people who want to restore their communication score will report you for no reason, and this can lower your communication score. I ask that you review my request and at least make some changes to the communication score system. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No Description A question for any developer or person in charge of the Comms/BH score system: Why does Dota still have a Behavior Score requirement for being able to type, speak, or simply use pings more than a few times, when everyone already has the option to mute or ignore all text and voice communications from both teammates and enemies? Unfortunately, due to electrical problems in my country, I have been unable to communicate properly for over two years. I can’t type, speak, or even ping multiple times to warn my teammates about a gank or enemy movements. This system simply doesn’t make sense. Reducing or restricting communication in a MOBA is extremely detrimental to gameplay, especially when everyone already has the ability to filter messages or mute other players. Could someone at least clarify whether there are any plans to rework the Comms system or, at the very least, allow players to use pings at all times, with a cooldown limit of 10 Pings every 60 seconds ? Description Hello. I have been playing Dota 2 for a long time, and I am writing not to dispute a ban or complain about a specific match. I want to draw attention to a problem in the Communication Score and report system that, in my view, harms the game and punishes innocent players. I agree that Behavior Score is a working and necessary thing. It genuinely restrains those who ruin games: AFK players, feeders, people who intentionally spoil the match. But Communication Score works differently, and here is the fundamental problem. Dota 2 is a team game where communication is critical. When a player is forcibly deprived of the ability to write and speak, it is not only he who suffers, but also his four teammates. You cannot call missing, you cannot warn about a gank, you cannot call for Roshan, you cannot coordinate a push. So the punishment of one person turns into a punishment for the entire team. At the same time, the game already has a mute button. Any player can mute any teammate or opponent and no longer see or hear them. It turns out that the forced silence system duplicates a function that every player already has, but does it for everyone at once, without their consent. A separate problem is the mechanism of reports for communication itself. It does not analyze what exactly a person wrote or said. A report triggers based on the number of complaints. Because of this, a "communication report" easily turns into a tool of revenge: a person can be reported for bad play, for an incomprehensible move, for disagreeing with someone's decision- and he will receive a silence, even though he insulted no one. This has been discussed in the community for a long time, including by well-known players and streamers. Dendi publicly said that the report system "just doesn't work"; Stray228 compared forced mute in a team game to a situation where a footballer is left on the field but forbidden to pass. So on paper, the idea of separating "behavior" and "communication" looks logical. The problem is in the execution: the system triggers too easily on false complaints and gives a normal player almost no opportunity to prove that he did nothing wrong. What, in my opinion, should be changed: 1)Remove the forced global mute, or at least make it "off by default," so that teammates can decide for themselves whether to hear this player or not. 2)Make it so that a communication report triggers only with real analysis of text or voice, and not based on the number of complaints. 3)Leave players under silence with basic pings and the chat wheel- they are not toxicity and are needed for the game. 4)Return reports to their original meaning: to punish for ruining the game, not for an "unpleasant manner of communication." I understand that this is not a technical support issue, but I ask you to forward this to the Dota 2 team. Thank you for the game and for actually reading feedback. Ability name Doom ### Description **Patch:** 7.41f Doom's ultimate ability `Doom` can be cast on an allied hero **only if that hero is also Doom** (mirror matchup). On any other allied hero, the ability correctly fails to cast. When cast on an allied Doom, the ability applies the full `Doom` debuff: complete mute (no abilities, no items) and healing prevention. The ally also takes periodic damage from the Aghanim's Scepter aura, which incorrectly treats them as an enemy. The ability can also be cast on **regular creeps** (lane and neutral) regardless of the matchup. It applies the debuff and periodic damage. Ancient creeps and Roshan correctly reject the cast. ### Expected behavior Doom should not be castable on any allied hero or any non-hero unit. The fact that it only works on an allied Doom and on regular creeps proves this is a targeting validation bug, not intended behavior. ### Steps to reproduce **Reproduce on allied Doom:** 1. Pick Doom in Demo Mode with a second Doom as an ally (mirror matchup). 2. Buy Aghanim's Scepter. 3. Target the allied Doom with your ultimate. 4. Ability casts successfully, ally Doom gets muted and takes aura damage. **Reproduce on a creep (neutral or lane):** 1. Pick Doom in Demo Mode. 2. Target a regular lane or neutral creep (not Ancient). 3. Ability casts successfully, creep gets Doom debuff and periodic damage. ### Note - The creep bug works both **with and without** Aghanim's Scepter. - The ally-Doom bug only occurs when Aghanim's Support (Ari) directed me to post this here because the current Behavior Score system has a fundamental design flaw at the ~3k level. The way the communication ban interacts with automated reports creates an impossible, inescapable loop for players who are genuinely trying to win and improve their score. **The Core Design Flaw: Playing with Bots** Communication is the absolute core of any multiplayer team game. When you completely remove a player's ability to communicate, you turn a team-based strategic game into a single-player experience. I might as well be playing against bots, because the interaction with my team is exactly the same. When you drop below 6,000 behavior score, you cannot ask for help, coordinate with your team, ping the map effectively, or explain macro decisions. Because you cannot explain your actions, teammates lacking map awareness automatically assume you are griefing, report you, and the automated system issues severe punishments with zero human oversight. **Case Study from a Recent Match:** To demonstrate how this algorithm fails, here is exactly what happened in my recent match. I played Axe offlane with a Phoenix support against a very tough Spectre and Enchantress lane. Phoenix was role-abusing, taking farm and last hits instead of helping me survive. From a gameplay design perspective, what is the intended correct play here? - **Option A:** Stand at a safe distance on the lane, get zero gold, and leech experience from my support (who can safely solo the lane due to range and escape skills). This is widely considered griefing. - **Option B:** Leave the unplayable lane, move to the jungle to recover, and let the support have the lane. I chose Option B. I stopped contesting Phoenix for farm and went to jungle. Because I was completely muted by the system, I couldn't tell my team why I was doing this. Here is how the situation escalated: - Phoenix followed me to the jungle to steal last hits from a triple-stacked camp I made. - He/she then moved to the safe lane to stand in trees, doing nothing, but to leech XP from our carries. - He/she went in to bushes to AFK for about 15 seconds from a middle of teamfight with full hp. I ended up doing the supports (Phoenix) work, buying 3 Observers and 6 Sentries, while the actual support bought exactly 2 Sentries in a 42-minute game. I also made several immediate buybacks after dying. Again, because I was muted, I couldn't explain that this was a deliberate macro strategy. Returning to the lane meant instant death from Spectre and Enchantress. Buying back allowed me to farm safer areas and stay close to the game's overall XP progression. The scoreboard at the end of the game proves this strategy worked: I successfully kept up with the level progression and was on the exact same level as everyone else. Once I got the relevant basic items (Vanguard, Blink Dagger to counter the 4 ranged enemies, and a Blade Mail), I rotated back, tanked damage, initiated fights, and we actually won the game. I was even commended by our carries. **The Automated Punishment & The Single Draft Trap:** Despite adapting to a griefing teammate, buying the wards, playing to the very end, and winning the game, the automated system immediately hit me with a 4-hour matchmaking ban, a -500 behavior score drop, and a Low Priority penalty requiring 3 Single Draft wins to escape. This Single Draft penalty is completely contradictory and feeds directly into the same broken loop: - You are forced to play with actual, legitimate griefers who are in Low Priority for the right reasons. - Because the hero pool is restricted, teammates frequently pick unsuitable heroes for the lineup, leading to setups with 4 or 5 hard carries. - People refuse to adapt their roles, or they simply have never played the random heroes they were given. - This inevitably leads to more griefing, ruined games, and consequently, more false reports from tilted teammates. - As a result, your behavior score continues to tank even further based on false reports while you are just trying to win your 3 mandatory matches. I am a 37-year-old man, and I do not believe I have ever been a toxic player. I do not throw rage fits, and I have never abandoned a match midway through unless there was a power outage (which hasn't happened in years). I am a team player—in non-role queue games, if everyone else picks a carry or a tank, I will always try to pick a support or whatever role the team is missing. To be completely honest, I do not even remember why my behavior score originally dropped to ~3000, because it happened several years ago. Since then, due to how this communication ban and punishment loop operates, it has been practically impossible to raise it back up. **The Mathematical Impossibility:** The most broken part of this system is the math behind recovering your score: - **The Grind:** If you manage to play 15 games without a single negative ping or false report, the system updates your score by about 250 points. That is roughly 12.5 hours of playing. - **The Punishment:** After this single match—where I didn't communicate at all, adapted to a bad lane, and won the game—I lost 500 points. - **The Result:** 25 hours of clean grinding wiped out by an automated algorithm in an instant. My score dropped back to 2,500. Now, on top of a 4-hour ban and the Single Draft prison, I am forced to play AT LEAST another 25 hours of unranked games just to unlock ranked matchmaking again, just for the exact same problem to repeat. **The "For Fun" Report Exploit:** The vulnerability of this automated system is public knowledge. There are multiple YouTube videos right now showing players admitting they report others purely for fun. They proudly showcase their "Action Taken" lists on screen, openly acknowledging that none of the players they reported actually did anything wrong—yet your automated system still punishes those innocent players based on malicious reports. **Conclusion** I completely understand that a multiplayer game needs a punishment system to keep the community healthy, but this current implementation is absolutely not the right way to do it. You are simply riding on the legend of the game at this point. This fundamentally broken system is undoubtedly driving many dedicated players to League of Legends, and I am now one of them. Description There is a critical logical flaw in the automated Behavior Score system that causes a permanent soft-lock for solo queue players trapped below 3000 score. For the past 6 months, my account has been completely restricted from ranked matchmaking, voice chat, and text chat. Despite being physically unable to commit any communication abuse (due to the permanent system mute), my behavior score continues to drop or remains frozen at the absolute bottom. The automated system aggregates all reports blindly without assessing context. In low behavior brackets, solo queue players are constantly matched with pre-made party stacks (2, 3, or 4 players). When a party loses a match, they subjectively use the silent solo player as a scapegoat, issuing 3 to 4 reports simultaneously out of spite. The system treats this mass party report as a consensus of toxic behavior. This creates an inescapable mathematical deadlock: 1. To increase the behavior score, a player must play standard matches. 2. Playing standard matches as a solo queue player naturally triggers false, subjective reports from toxic party stacks. 3. The automated system accepts these reports (even for communication abuse on a completely muted account), lowering the score even further. Currently, the only way to escape this automated prison is to break Steam's ToS by paying third-party boosting services to play in a 5-man stack where reports are impossible. This is a technical system loop that cannot be resolved automatically. I kindly request a developer or technical administrator to review my account logs for the past 6 months, verify that I have not committed any genuine griefing (destroying items, running down mid), and manually adjust or reset my behavior score to a baseline level. Description The current Communication/Behavior Score system and its automated in-game mutes are actively hurting the matchmaking experience. Dota 2 is a highly competitive, team-oriented game that requires constant communication. The problems with the current mute system are: 1. System Abuse: The automated mute system is easily abused. Players frequently use communication reports to punish teammates for bad gameplay (missed spells, lost lanes), rather than actual toxicity. 2. Collateral Damage: A globally muted player cannot coordinate with their team (calling missing, Roshan timings, smoke ganks). This essentially punishes the 4 other innocent players on the team who are now playing at a severe disadvantage. 3. Impossible to Recover: Once a player's communication score drops, it is incredibly difficult to raise it back up because they cannot communicate to be commended, creating a vicious cycle. Suggested changes to rework the system: - Replace the forced absolute mute with a "soft mute". By default, the player is muted, but teammates should have a clear button to manually UNMUTE them if they want to coordinate. - Do not restrict essential gameplay pings and basic chat wheel commands for muted players. - Rework the automated penalty system so that report volume alone doesn't trigger immediate, severe communication bans without actual text/voice chat analysis. is a long-standing and very frustrating issue in Dota 2 related to the communication system and the Behavior Score system. When a player has a low behavior score, is in low priority, or is in a muted/punished chat pool (due to reports), the in-game chat becomes restricted or disabled. As a result, the /roll command (which generates a random number to resolve disputes) stops working in all modes, including normal non-role queue matches (All Pick without strict role assignment). What this leads to: Draft Chaos. When two players both want to play mid (or carry/offlane), they have no fair way to decide who gets the role. Double Mid Syndrome. Since /roll is unavailable, players just lock a second mid hero anyway, turning the game into a toxic mess from minute zero. Game Ruining. Instead of a civilized resolution, arguments escalate, players start flaming each other, and often intentionally feed or grief because the dispute is only resolved by "who picks faster". Inequality. This issue disproportionately affects players with low behavior scores — who are already in a bad spot. Instead of giving them tools to resolve conflicts peacefully (like rolling), the system takes that tool away, making matches even more unbearable and preventing them from recovering their score. The Core Problem: /roll is NOT a social chat message; it is a gameplay mechanic (a console/chat command) that returns a random integer. Muting chat or restricting communication should not affect gameplay commands, especially in non-role queue modes where /roll is the only civilized way to distribute roles. Proposed Solution: Make the /roll command available regardless of "Low Priority", "Muted", or "Low Behavior Score" status. Alternatively, add a "Roll" button directly to the hero selection UI that is always functional (similar to how it works in tournament/captain's mode drafts or custom lobbies). This is a critical quality-of-life improvement for the community that would significantly reduce toxicity and the number of ruined In ranked games, I play the roles assigned to me by the matchmaking system and try to play for the win. I also support Dota 2 financially and enjoy the game, which is why I would like to understand how this system works and how it could potentially be improved. I recently checked my Steam Personal Game Data → Dota 2 → Account → Incoming Match Player Report. My recent data shows Communication Reports even during periods where I had no abandons or excessive reports. For example: August 11: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 3 Communication Reports from 2 reporting parties August 8: - 15 matches - 14 positive matches - 1 reported match - 0 abandons - 4 Communication Reports from 3 reporting parties August 6: - 15 matches - 11 positive matches - 4 reported matches - 0 abandons - 7 total reports - 4 Communication Reports from 4 reporting parties August 2: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 0 Communication Reports My main question is: How can a player have a maximum Behavior Score of 12,000/12,000 while having a Communication Score of only 5,800/12,000? I understand that these are separate systems and that Communication Reports can affect Communication Score. However, I am concerned about the possibility of unjustified or retaliatory reports. There is another situation that I believe is worth considering. In a five-player team, it is possible that three players are in the same party and know each other. If one of these players has a disagreement with me, the other two party members may potentially report me simply to support their friend, even if they did not personally witness any actual communication violation. In this situation, what could start as a disagreement between two players could potentially result in multiple reports against the same player simply because several players are grouped together. For example, instead of receiving one report from the player involved in the disagreement, I could potentially receive reports from all three members of the party because they want to support their friend. This raises an important question: Does the Communication Score system take party relationships or coordinated/retaliatory reporting into account? If multiple members of the same party report the same player, are these reports treated completely independently, or does the system recognize that they may be related to the same incident? I believe this is important because otherwise a single conflict between two players could potentially have a disproportionately large effect on another player's Communication Score. Players can report each other because of disagreements, frustration after losing a game, disagreements about gameplay decisions, or personal conflicts. Therefore, I would like to understand how the system prevents abuse of Communication Reports. I contacted Steam Support about this issue. They told me that the scores are automated and that Steam Support cannot manually adjust them. They also stated that they do not provide additional information about how the behavior scoring system is calculated. They recommended that I bring this issue to the Dota 2 community and development forums. So this is what I am doing. I am NOT asking for my Communication Score to be manually increased. I would simply like to understand whether the current system can incorrectly penalize a player because of unjustified, retaliatory, or potentially coordinated Communication Reports, and whether there are mechanisms that prevent players from abusing the reporting system. I would also like to raise another question regarding the recovery of Communication Score. Why does the Communication Score not have some form of regular recalibration or review period, for example once a year? Would it be possible to introduce an annual recalibration, review, or another mechanism that would give players who have demonstrated consistently good behavior over a long period of time a clearer way to recover their Communication Score? In my subjective opinion, there appears to be a significant imbalance between losing Communication Score and recovering it. It feels like a player can receive Communication Reports relatively easily and potentially lose Communication Score very quickly, while recovering that lost score through consistently good behavior appears to be much slower. Even if a player makes a serious effort to communicate politely and avoid violations over a long period of time, recovering from a low Communication Score can feel extremely difficult. In other words, the negative effect of reports can appear very quickly, while the positive effect of consistently good behavior takes much longer to become visible. I believe that a regular recalibration or another transparent recovery mechanism could make the system feel more fair. It would also give players a clearer motivation to improve their behavior because they would know that consistently good behavior over time can meaningfully restore their Communication Score. If there is no way for players to verify whether reports against them were legitimate, how can they know what behavior they need to change? I would appreciate any clarification from the Dota 2 developers or experienced players who understand how the current system works. I am not asking for special treatment for my account. Description ### Summary The current report and communication score system in Dota 2 feels too passive. Bad actors can severely insult opponents in All-Chat, ruin everyone's emotional state, and they only receive a minor score deduction matches later. We need a firmer, faster, and more transparent approach to protect the player base from toxicity. ### Why we need this (Balancing Environment and Player Retention) We understand that Valve needs to maintain its player base. Permanently banning or suspending accounts for chat toxicity can be counterproductive, as it drives players away entirely and ruins matchmaking times. Instead of banning the account, we should strictly "strip away their ability to ruin the game environment" while still letting them play the game. Keeping them in the game but forcing them into silence is the perfect balance for player retention and community health. ### Proposed Solutions 1. **Immediate All-Chat Time-out (Real-time Mitigation):** If the system detects severe toxic keywords or verified report spikes in All-Chat, that player should be instantly and automatically muted from All-Chat for the rest of the match or the next 24 hours. Stop the toxicity in its tracks before it spreads to other players. 2. **100% Automated System Reading (No Human Check Needed):** The system should automatically scan all chat logs using a pre-defined blocklist of toxic words, slurs, and toxic gaming jargon (e.g., "ez", "noob", "trash", "dog", etc.). There is no need for manual human checkers. If the text matches the filter, the penalty is executed immediately by the server. 3. **The "First-Striker" Principle (Protecting Those Who Reply):** Often, a toxic player starts the insults, and their teammates or opponents only reply out of frustration. The system should only punish the **first person** who initiates the toxic behavior in that specific chat timeline. Anyone who replies or defends themselves afterwards should NOT be penalized. Punishing the "first striker" stops the root cause of the toxicity without unfairly striking back at victims who are just reacting to provocation. 4. **Heavier Penalties for Severe Insults (-2000 Score):** Ruinous behavior shouldn't cost just 100 points. Severe toxic words should trigger a massive, immediate deduction (e.g., -2000 communication score). Since players lose All-Chat privileges when dropping below 10,000 points, one single toxic outburst should instantly silence them for dozens of matches until they earn it back. 5. **Transparency (Show the Evidence Log):** When players lose score, the client should show them a notification displaying exactly which log/words triggered the penalty. They need to know precisely *what* they typed that led to the punishment. Winning a game shouldn't be an excuse to demean opponents. Respecting the enemy team is basic sportsmanship, and Valve can enforce it strictly through precise, heavy chat restrictions without having to ban players from playing. ### Example Match ID (and Description ​The current Behavior Score system is detrimental to the Dota 2 experience. It fails to distinguish between unavoidable technical issues (power/internet outages, hardware failures) and intentional disruptive behavior. As a result, players are trapped in a "point of no return," where recovery is nearly impossible. ​The game is fundamentally a team-based experience, yet this system forces players into a state of "silent survival." Players are now terrified to use voice or text chat to coordinate, as any interaction can trigger retaliatory reports from teammates. This silence destroys the core of Dota 2, as communication is essential for team play. ​Furthermore, this system drives players to abandon their main accounts and create new ones, which devalues the competitive integrity of the game. ​Proposed Reforms: ​Remove the Hidden Behavior Score: Replace the current hidden point system with a transparent and predictable disciplinary model. ​Clear Penalties for Abandoning: Instead of a complex score reduction, implement direct consequences for technical issues. For example: 3 abandons = 5 games of Low Priority. ​Targeted Communication Bans: If a player receives reports from all 9 other players in a single match, they should receive a 48-hour communication ban. If the behavior persists, the punishment should escalate to Low Priority matches without access to chat for the purpose of "correction." ​Low Priority Revamp: Replace the mandatory "Single Draft" (SD) mode in Low Priority with "All Random" (AR). This makes the punishment less monotonous and keeps the game engaging, even for those serving time. ​Address Report Abuse and the Overwatch System: The current report system is heavily abused as a weapon against teammates. Furthermore, the "Overwatch" system is ineffective because reviewers often lack context or are biased, leading to unfair judgments. We need a system that filters out malicious, weaponized reports rather than penalizing any form of communication. ​The goal should be to encourage positive communication and team play, not to force players into "mute mode" or drive them away from the game entirely. I urge the development team to reconsider the current model in favor of a more transparent and fair disciplinary framework. Description # **The Current Player Behavior System Creates Silent Matches and Makes Recovery Nearly Impossible** I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I believe the current Player Behavior Summary system has serious flaws that are damaging the quality of matches and the social experience of the game. For nearly a year, my Behavior Score has remained around 3000. During this time, I have had very limited communication privileges, rarely communicate with other players, do not abandon matches, and do not intentionally grief games. Despite this, my score barely changes and meaningful recovery appears almost impossible. The main issue is that the system does not seem to adequately distinguish between intentional griefing and simply having a bad game. When a team loses, frustrated players often report their teammates. A player can make mistakes, have a poor performance, or simply be unlucky without intentionally ruining the match. However, those reports still contribute to a punishment system that can trap players at low Behavior Scores for extremely long periods of time. Another consequence is that many matches have become completely silent. Players are afraid to communicate because they fear reports and further penalties. Others have already lost access to communication features. As a result, matches often contain: * No leadership * No strategic discussion * No coordination * No planning * No meaningful social interaction Dota 2 is fundamentally a team game. Communication is one of its most important elements. A system designed to improve player behavior should not create an environment where players are afraid to speak. My questions to the Dota team are: 1. How does the system distinguish between intentional griefing and simply performing poorly? 2. How is a player expected to recover from a very low Behavior Score if reports continue to outweigh positive behavior? 3. Is the current system achieving its intended goal, or is it simply creating silent matches where players avoid communication altogether? I understand the need to punish toxic behavior, intentional griefing, and abusive communication. However, the current system appears excessively punitive and offers very little transparency regarding how players can realistically recover. I hope the Dota team will review the long-term effects of this system and consider whether it is truly improving the player experience or unintentionally harming it. # The Current Player Behavior System Creates Silent Matches and Makes Recovery Nearly Impossible I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I believe the current Player Behavior Summary system has serious flaws that are damaging the quality of matches and the social experience of the game. Description 1. Current Problem The quick chat wheel is the main tool for communicating with allies. However, it is often ineffective because: Many players ignore the chat. Some use "allmute" and disable chat entirely. Result: Until you reach a high rank, requests for help are frequently ignored. This negatively affects the overall gameplay experience, especially for lower MMR players. 2. Proposed Solution Add an option to send a visible notification to all allies when a player needs assistance, similar to the notification that appears when a teammate purchases a key item. How it would work: A player can request help from the entire team. The request can be sent once every N seconds (to prevent spam). The notification appears in a prominent on-screen window, just like important item purchase alerts. 3. Expected Benefits Provides a clear and obvious signal even for players with low MMR or those who mute chat. Partially reduces the impact of unresponsive teammates. Encourages players to think about teamplay opportunities and respond to calls for help. 4. Additional Notes This system would not replace normal communication, but would serve as a reliable complement to existing tools. The cooldown limit would prevent notification spam. because the frequency of such players appearing is abnormally high • Winning matches also present a problem Many games are heavily dominated by one player who is clearly far above the current bracket, effectively deciding the outcome early These “free wins” provide no real gameplay experience either What I want to emphasize is: I am not asking to win every game, and I do not expect perfect fairness However, the core of Dota 2 is competition, back-and-forth play, and strategic depth Right now, the outcome of many matches is no longer determined by fair team competition, but by extreme differences Description Адресат: Valve / команда разработки Dota 2 Настоящим мы обращаемся с требованием полного удаления системы Communication Score из Dota 2 как системно неисправной и наносящей прямой вред качеству игры. Данный вывод сделан не на основании единичного инцидента, а по итогам многолетнего использования системы и массовой реакции игрового сообщества. За годы существования Communication Score на форуме Steam были созданы тысячи тем, в которых игроки независимо друг от друга описывают одни и те же проблемы: непрозрачность, непредсказуемость наказаний и отсутствие реального пути восстановления. Ключевые проблемы системы Отсутствие проверки содержания коммуникации Система опирается на репорты, которые не проходят валидацию по содержанию. Она не различает токсичное поведение, активную игровую коммуникацию и просто обильное общение. В результате наказываются не только токсичные игроки, но и: новички, активно задающие вопросы; лидеры, дающие коллы и координирующие команду; любые «заметные» игроки, чаще взаимодействующие с командой. Непрозрачный и нестабильный вес репортов Репорты имеют неочевидный и непредсказуемый вес. В одних случаях несколько репортов не приводят к заметным последствиям, в других — один репорт способен вызвать резкое падение Communication Score (сотни или тысячи очков) без объяснения причин. Это делает систему недоверяемой и невоспроизводимой. Наказания без причинно-следственной связи На практике фиксируются случаи, когда репорты от игроков вражеской команды применяются даже при отсутствии токсичной коммуникации. Репорт может быть следствием поражения и эмоциональной реакции, но система не отличает такие ситуации от реальных нарушений. Отсутствие работающего механизма восстановления Даже при сотнях матчей, положительной статистике, минимальном количестве репортов и большом числе лайков Communication Score может: не расти месяцами; обрушиваться за несколько игр без объяснимых причин. Это означает, что система не имеет корректного «конечного состояния выхода» из наказания. Критический ущерб командной игре и соревновательной целостности Автоматические мьюты: напрямую ухудшают качество матчей; лишают команды координации; влияют на исходы побед и поражений. Особенно критично это в premade-группах. Игроки объединяются в группы именно для командной игры и координации. Любые автоматические ограничения общения в таких условиях противоречат самой цели групповой игры и наносят максимальный ущерб. Избыточность системы В Dota 2 уже существуют достаточные и эффективные инструменты индивидуальной фильтрации: mute, ignore, отключение чата и голосовой связи. Эти инструменты позволяют каждому игроку самостоятельно решать, кого он хочет слышать, не нарушая симметрию матчей и не ограничивая остальных. Communication Score не добавляет новой ценности и дублирует функции, уже реализованные более корректно. Деградация коммуникационной среды за годы использования За более чем три года существования Communication Score: токсичность в игре не была устранена; при этом нормальная, полезная командная коммуникация практически исчезла. Игроки массово предпочитают молчать из страха получить репорт, даже когда общение повышает шансы на победу. Это подтверждается как личным опытом, так и тысячами обсуждений на официальном форуме Steam. Description Addressee: Valve / Dota 2 Development Team We hereby request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a fundamentally flawed system that causes direct harm to match quality. This conclusion is not based on an isolated incident. It is the result of years of real-world use and extensive community feedback. Over the lifetime of Communication Score, thousands of forum threads have been created on Steam, consistently describing the same issues: lack of transparency, unpredictable penalties, and the absence of a reliable recovery mechanism. Core issues No validation of communication content The system relies on reports without validating the actual content of communication. It does not distinguish between toxicity, active gameplay coordination, and frequent but neutral communication. As a result, it punishes: new players asking questions, team leaders making calls, any highly visible or communicative player. Opaque and inconsistent report weighting Reports have an unclear and inconsistent impact. Multiple reports may have little effect, while in other cases a single report can cause a massive score drop without explanation. This makes the system non-transparent and unreliable. Punishment without causal connection Reports from opposing players can be applied even when no toxic communication occurred. Emotion-driven reports after a loss are not filtered or distinguished from legitimate cases. No functional recovery path Even after hundreds of matches with positive behavior, minimal reports, and many commendations, the Communication Score may: stagnate indefinitely; collapse within a few matches. This indicates the absence of a valid recovery endpoint. Direct damage to competitive integrity Automatic mutes: reduce match quality, break team coordination, directly affect win and loss outcomes. This is especially damaging in premade groups, where communication is the primary reason players group up. Any automatic communication restriction in such cases contradicts the purpose of team play. System redundancy Dota 2 already provides effective individual filtering tools such as mute and ignore. These tools allow players to manage their own experience without breaking match symmetry. Communication Score adds no unique value. Long-term degradation of communication After more than three years of use: toxicity has not been eliminated, meaningful team communication has largely disappeared. Players increasingly choose silence out of fear of reports, even when communication would improve gameplay. This trend is widely documented across the Steam community. Request For the reasons stated above, we request the complete removal of the Communication Score system from Dota 2 as a system that is: structurally irreparable, opaque and unpredictable, redundant, status** Complete silence and ignoring from Valve **What became clear after the discussion** Based on the discussion in this thread, the analysis of other topics, and publicly available information, it became obvious that the problem is not about isolated "edge cases" or specific numbers. This is about the system logic itself and its impact on teamplay . In its current implementation, Communication Score in the long run is primarily driven by report and mute statistics , not by the actual quality or context of communication. At the same time, text and voice analysis is mostly used for fast punishments (mutes) , but it does not solve the problem of cumulative score degradation . **Why staying silent does not protect you** Silence is not a protection, because the "Politeness" score can decrease even when there is no communication at all . This means a complete absence of any interaction: no pings, no voice chat, no text messages . By design, the "Politeness" metric is supposed to reflect the quality of communication . In practice, however, it can change without any communication happening . In other words, a metric tied to communication continues to drop even when communication does not exist. **Main problem: the system breaks teamplay** The core issue is that the system restricts communication without addressing the root causes of conflicts. When the score drops, a player loses the ability to interact properly with the team, while still being placed into matches where communication is critically important . In Dota, communication is not a bonus or a "nice-to-have feature". It is the foundation of team-based gameplay . Calls, timings, cooldown information, and positioning directly affect fights and match outcomes. When part of the team is restricted, the match loses symmetry of conditions , and overall match quality degrades for everyone. In practice it looks like this: you see an opportunity for coordinated action, but due to restrictions you cannot call a timing or request support. Coordination is replaced by guessing and randomness . Even with high "politeness" values, some players remain restricted, while others avoid active communication because of fear of reports . As a result, communication becomes one-sided or disappears completely. **What I propose to discuss in this thread** The real question is no longer about how to "recover" or "farm" politeness score. The question is: why does the game have a system that in its current form does not improve behavior , but instead limits a core gameplay tool and reduces match quality . My assumption is that this system was introduced to increase retention and inflate online numbers. Players tolerated it for several years. That patience is gone. **I propose to focus the discussion on this: the system logic , its transparency , and its impact on the match as a whole . And whether it should be fundamentally reworked or ##disabled. Without a radical redesign, the "Politeness" system causes more harm than benefit.** Main link to the topic - https://steamcommunity.com/app/570/discussions/0/705506553887738727/ It's time for VALVE to wake up **Внимание!** Система вежливости является системой удерживания игркоов, а не борьбы с токсичностью **Что стало понятно по итогам обсуждения** По результатам обсуждения в этом топике, анализа других тем и доступной информации стало очевидно, что проблема не сводится к отдельным "частным случаям" или конкретным цифрам. Речь идет о логике работы системы и ее влиянии на командную игру . В текущей реализации communication score в долгосрочной перспективе в первую очередь зависит от статистики репортов и мутов , а не от качества и контекста коммуникации. При этом анализ текста и голоса используется в основном для быстрых санкций (мутов) , но не решает проблему накопительного падения показателя . **Почему молчание не защищает** Молчание не является защитой, потому что показатель "Вежливости" может снижаться даже при полном отсутствии коммуникации . Речь идет именно об отсутствии любой информации от игрока: нет пингов, нет голосового чата, нет текстовых сообщений . При этом "Вежливость" по своему назначению должна отражать качество коммуникации . Но на практике она может изменяться без самой коммуникации как таковой . То есть показатель, связанный исключительно с общением, может продолжить снижаться даже тогда, когда общения просто не существует. **Главная проблема: система ломает командную игру** Ключевая проблема в том, что система ограничивает коммуникацию , не устраняя первопричины конфликтов. При падении показателя игрок лишается возможности полноценно взаимодействовать с командой, но при этом продолжает играть в матчах, где коммуникация критически важна . В Dota коммуникация - это не бонус и не "приятная опция", а основа командной игры . Коллы, тайминги, информация о кулдаунах и позициях напрямую влияют на исход драк и матча. Когда часть команды ограничена в общении, матч теряет симметрию условий , и качество игры падает для всех. На практике это выглядит так: ты видишь момент для совместных действий, но из-за ограничений не можешь обозначить тайминг или запросить поддержку. Координация заменяется угадыванием и везением . Даже при высоких значениях "вежливости" часть команды может сидеть под ограничениями, а другая часть начинает избегать активного общения из-за страха репортов . В итоге коммуникация становится односторонней либо исчезает полностью. **Что предлагаю обсуждать в теме** Поэтому вопрос уже не в том, как "поднять" или "отмыть" вежливость. Вопрос в другом: зачем в игре существует система, которая в текущем виде не исправляет поведение , а ограничивает ключевой инструмент и ухудшает качество матчей . Мое предположение, что систему сделали, для удержания и повышение онлайна. Мы терпели эту систему несколько лет, терпение кончилось. **Предлагаю обсуждать именно это: логику системы , прозрачность и влияние на матч в целом . И как ее исправить, или отключить. Description This system needs a rework for the reasons i've listed below: **1. Commends have no weight** It appears that no matter how many commends you get after a match, 5, 10, 15, etc. - they do not increase your behavior score, yet a single report could decrease it by 150 points. Reports have a lot more weight than commends even though it's just as easy to report someone as it is to commend them. This inequality makes it easier to lose your behavior score and stunts your progress to regain it. **2. Inability to stop an abandon/AFK** Having a behavior score of less than 5k makes you more susceptible to losing because you have no way to prevent a player from going afk as a result of disconnecting. As a result the team with a disconnected player has a serious disadvantage over the team that has no players that disconnected. Keep in mind that can also apply to you if you disconnect, because you get thrown in a pool of players that have the same or lower behavior score than you. **3.Unnecessary mutes** You can mute a toxic player in the scoreboard if you want, both their voice chat and text chat by clicking a few buttons. If anything permanently muting a pool of players only hurts teamplay by making them unable to make game-saving calls. **4. Description this is what ai said about your stupid broken system Dota 2's behavior system is widely considered "broken" by players because it creates toxic matchmaking trenches, disproportionately punishes good players through malicious reports (especially in lower tiers), struggles to differentiate genuine griefing from disagreements or off-meta plays, and heavily penalizes communication/abandonments more than it rewards positive behavior, leading to frustratingly low scores and unfair match quality. Key issues include unlimited reports, the impact of reports in casual games (like Turbo) affecting Ranked, and an inability to climb out of low-score pools once there. Core Problems with the Behavior Score System: Abuse of Reports: Players can report teammates for minor infractions (losing roll, missing spells, bad plays), and these reports count heavily, even if unverified by Overwatch. The "Trench" Effect: Lower behavior scores lead to more reports from other low-score players, creating a cycle where it's extremely hard to climb out, even with good behavior. Disproportionate Penalties: A few bad games (or even just power outages/bad internet) can tank a score, while regaining points through commends or positive games is slow and difficult. Unfair Punishment for Communication: The Communication Score (Comms Score) is highly sensitive; arguments or frustration in 15% of games can drop it significantly, forcing mutes and hindering team play, while positive play yields few points. Lack of Differentiation: Reports from Turbo (casual) games carry the same weight as Ranked, leading to casual abuse. System Imbalance: Reports and abandons often feel weighted far more heavily than commends, making positive actions insufficient to offset negatives. Player Experiences & Frustrations: Players report losing thousands of points for technical issues or bad luck, feeling unfairly punished for issues beyond their control. Good players get stuck in low-score pools with genuinely toxic players (feeders, intentional griefers) because the system segregates them. Many feel the system doesn't encourage improvement but rather punishes mistakes or perceived lack of meta adherence. In essence, while intended to isolate toxic players, the current behavior system often punishes good players who have bad luck, experience technical issues, or get caught in cycles of malicious Ability name Anything Pure damage, Ransack, Arcane Orb, Diabolic Edict, Golem Pure Fists etc ### Description I love to play Dota - I have played over 10, 000 games!!!! Every year more and more the game comes into balance. There are still some key heroes that are still too strong and are avoiding enough balance changes. With all these games I have noticed many themes that repeat and I will usually almost NEVER win against them. We also need to address the PURE DAMAGE mechanic being too strong. I have assembled a balance patch to address this and the reasons why. Lets start with Leshrac with this match ID 8535789981 - Legend 3.1k bracket lasting only 23 minutes! The Leshrac ends the game 23 - 3. Any hero dies INSTANTLY to his combo towards the end of the game. FYI in the last 200 games there has never been a ranked match that ended before 30 minutes. Before level 6 he just walks up on repeat and tanks the tower hitting me for way too much damage - there is nothing I can do my heroes all have spells with cooldowns but Leshrac has diabolic edict with a very long up time. Suggested fix: For the early game remove the talent Misanthropy - pushing towers with Lesh is dead for a long time - so that talent just makes him stronger for free. For all game change diabolic edict to Magical so players can mitigate the damage. The duration of diabolic edict change to scale length based on level so lv1 4 second duration, lv2 5, lv3 7, lv4 10 sec duration. Another suggested solution is to nerf his movement speed from 325 to 290 - there is simply no need for this hero to be so fast and own the game with a mana boots. Death Prophet - this hero is designed poorly and is the most durable hero in the game, no weak phase. You can see from the match ID she is often unkillable and this needs a fix: 8545476334 - I think if we remove the item eternal shroud things should come into balance - that item gives insane value for the price - less than 4000 gold for an item that gives 20% magic resist - 500 hp almost and further magic resist over time??? No way that item has to go. Even as mid any ability to beat her is thwarted by the bottle - the random rune spawn chance also is a problem and should be addressed. For a strategy game the amount of luck happening with the runes should be fixed. Lone Druid - The bear has too much hp from the start - it has no weak phase in the game. A Lone druid mid will always dominate - Dota should be a game focused on skill so I suggest we need to fix any hero that can dominate especially early on. The bear starts out with 1100 hp at level 1 - no hero does this - there is no counter play to this because your spells are level 1 or 2 and the bear heals and is denying your creeps and bullying you out of the lane. There is no weakness to this. Bug?: The Spirit Bear shows a stat gain of 0 across all fields, it states the bear has a max hp of 2000 but a level 30 bear has 4900 hp??? Why and how - there is no explanation from this it must be a CRITICAL bug and needs to be fixed. Suggested Fix: Change bear Hp from lv1 (1100 > 700) in balance with other heroes OR fix the bug giving it extra hp. Remove life steal completely so chipping the HP of the bear away with spells is rewarded. Remember we want to balance the early game - there should be no such thing as an early game hero in Dota - these make for uninteresting games that do not require skill. Make the cooldown to summon spirit bear start WHEN the bear dies. Outworld Destroyer - this hero can force denies on your range creep consistently on each creep wave with Astral Imprisonment this is too strong so he will always reach level 6 before you and as I said we want to remove the early game domination some heroes have and make it more about skill. More importantly his Arcane Orb is just too strong - he can easily deal 500 PURE damage PER HIT (1500 per second on good attack speed). I was playing tide hunter and his Arcane Orb was not being blocked at all by kraken shell. Suggested Fix: Cap the damage that Arcane Orb can do to 300 per hit or change damage type from pure to MAGICAL to fit in line with its name as being arcane and to help players mitigate the damage with magic resist. Again there is NO REASON he should have pure damage on his ability - Silencer's glaives were changed to magical and it's doing fine so for balance reason's OD should be balanced too. Puck - this hero is just TOO elusive with too much mobility and does TOO much damage - he can drag out a fight having players expend too much resources, and just when you think you've got him he will Euls and blink. He will also send the Illusory orb one way and go the opposite direction and teleport opposite to where you want. Suggested fix: Extend Blink dagger duration to 4 or 5 seconds to disable upon receiving hit damage, or if not then reduce phase shift to a flat 2 seconds, limit the maximum teleport range of illusory orb so puck can't go such massive distances in opposite. Axe - His blink initiation makes the game just too hard - a 3 second bkb piercing aoe stun on a 10 second cool down? He's so strong compared to other offlaners that immortal players say to climb out of 3k you MUST only play a select few offlaners - LC or Axe for their initiation etc. If you compare it to Tidehunter Axe is just better in every way more tankier and more fast paced game impact with a low cooldown ult being berserker's rage. Suggested solution: Remove the armor gain per kill OR reduce the stun duration to 2 seconds in line with most other stuns in the game. It should not pierce bkb etc OR if it keeps the 3 second duration it should not mute items so you can still use items like BKB etc which will protect you from the pure damage and culling blade effect. We have to keep axe in line with other Offlaners as having one or two heroes that are just better than the rest indicates a problem. Warlock - his ultimate and fatal bonds is too strong - more so than Witch Doctor and Disrupter because those other heroes have short duration but powerful ultimate's but what makes Warlock so strong is his Golem's last for way too long for an ultimate and create too much pressure and space within a team fight. They also dish out pure damage - again Dota can't be giving out pure damage for free there is no counter play. The fatal bonds sharing all this damage - it's just too much brain dead damage with no skill or drawback. In the middle of a team fight he is able to reliably land way too much damage, for way too long - this needs to be fixed. Suggested solution: The golem duration set to 15 second duration to fit in line with most other Dota abilities where you have a small window to use them. We can't have 60 second slow resistant, magic resistant, high hp, high damage units running around - that's not right it needs immediate fix. Their hp should fall to 2000 maximum, remove the level 25 80% magic resistance and 20 armor, replace with 10 second duration on Golem (maximum 25 seconds this way) and +2 second stun to first skill or +25% chance of 2 second stun from golems etc), remove slow resistance and change flaming fist from pure to magical. In addition remove fatal bonds completely - an 18 second AOE duration spell doing an additional 25% damage to multiple affected units is wrong for a skill. I suggest giving warlock a basic stun instead of 2 seconds OR at the very least change fatal bond duration to 6 seconds to fall in line with other abilities within the game. Beast Master - this hero wins EVERY game and our team just can't beat it - they are too strong in lane come online too fast and - their minions provide a free eye of skadi slow and he is able to end the game too fast. Suggested solution is to change primal roar from 4 second stun to 3 second stun and remove the slow completely. Also he ALWAYS rushes the Sceptre - the solution to fix this is to remove the +10 stacks gained from using Primal Roar and remove the healing given from the drums, the bonus damage per hit will be sufficient. Phantom Lancer - this hero requires specific counters and a good PL player rushes Heart, shard and aghs making him impossible to catch the real one and he is invisible. Having so much high hp makes the game easy. Another hero I rarely win against. This man can go all night long - which is against the norm for most heroes. Suggested solution: Remove the shard invisibility, remove the dispel he has - this is a flat no no - there is no basic dispel as an ability this must have been an oversight and change his ultimate to be an active that lasts 20 seconds with a cool down of 50 seconds so it has a 30 second down time to fit in line with other heroes. We have to be more understanding that a permanent up time ultimate is abusable. The illusions can be stronger during their 20 second window by way of taking less damage or dealing more damage but the 20 second window is required to fall in line with other heroes. Meepo - has always been strong - having 5 Units that all independently gain experience on an AGI hero means he will out level and be very tanky and he will force the game to end quicker than should be. The other problem is there is that PURE damage problem again - ransack deals pure damage for no reason and it's life steal. Suggested fix: remove mega meepo - the meepos are all very high hp tanky enemies with magic resistance, the success is to burst him down in team fights or catch one of his meepos out of position, he always has dig - he should not be able to drag his death out with Mega meepo. Change Ransack damage from pure to PHYSICAL. Change divided we stand magic resistance from 20% to 10%. Again he is too tanky and doesn't need more. Medusa - able to farm way too fast and hit multiple enemies, an ult that buys her more time to escape or deal more free damage - she is also notoriously difficult to kill because of the magic wand she carries. She completely countered my undying in lane - she should be able to go minus strength same as minus armour and die if enough decay stacks but I could no longer damage her in lane after getting her to 0 strength at all - completely countered me from the early game and I became useless in the later game.... Medusa also can flash farm - but doesn't buy bkb - this gives her an advantage over other carries that's a bit too much. Suggested solution: Just remove the mana shield and give her normal strength gain - Replace the mana shield with something else entirely perhaps an active ability that is similar to morphing wave form allowing her turn into a snake and slither 1000 units through the ground or something with a cool effect or perhaps the passive can be something akin to viper's attack slow etc. Making her need to buy BKB would help balance her in line other carries and this means she can't have full slots without any defensive items. Windranger - lucky last - this hero will get bkb so you can't blade mail and will now be permanently invisible. This basically guarantees a kill no brain no skill just blink and bkb and press ult and follow the hero you are killing. Suggested solution: remove the invisibility completely and damage reduction. Rework the scepter to something else entirely perhaps multi arrow shot with increased damage? Also increase the charge time for the arrow from 1 to 2 seconds. There is no balance in having a 1 second charge time skill that's long range deal 470 damage that's absurd. Change the arrow to 350 damage and make the sceptre deal 600 damage and throw three arrows with a small space between each other. Sand King - he has a reliable escape and buys blink and has one of the best ultimate's in the game. Bug: there appears to be a bug interaction with sentry where sand king can still hide and not be visible unless he is really close to the sentry - this needs to be fixed. Suggested solution: Remove the blind from sandstorm and increase invisibility fade after attacking to 1.3 seconds. The changes to blink dagger going on cooldown to 5 seconds as suggested earlier upon taking damage should balance this hero more. For epicenter remove the slow the damage and other effects are sufficient - you see most of the time sand king will blink then stun and ult you while right clicking - this is an insane amount of damage in such a short window and if you are slowed by 50% it's just too much so removing the slow will mean after you are stunned you can at least run. Sand storm duration should change to 12 seconds max duration to fall in line with other skills as having a 28 second duration spell on a 22 second cool down say WHAT? Again remove the blind. Queen Of Pain - picked in almost every game - in literally every role - the hero is too versatile - I will leave this up to the devs to sort this out however my suggested solution is the shadow strike is the problem - just looking at the skill it's a 16 second 55% slow on a 4 second cool down, provides tick damage and heals her??? That skill needs a full rework or at least it needs to remove some aspect such as the heal etc. The only other hero to have a slow this powerful is Veno and he is balanced by being very slow and squishy. QOP is a high mobility hero so this skill is a mistake design it's like having a Veno with this slow and high mobility. Pudge - this hero has way too much hp. He naturally buys shroud. Suggested solution: Consider just removing shroud from the game honestly, it provides too much hp + high magic resistance is not a combination we want to see in the game in one item. Make adjustments to flesh heap with 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 consider removing the facet flesh heap that gives him strength when he ults. Juggernaught - I rarely win against this hero - his blade fury does way too much damage, is a dispel and he is immune to stuns. His laning stage is very secure - no counter play and he has a healing ward. suggested solution: Make him move slower during blade fury or reduce duration so it scale with level 3, 4 and 5 seconds and reduce damage from 80 down to 50 scaling with level. Chaos Knight - this hero is strong in all stages just too strong. Suggested solution: make lifesteal at 20%. And a last note for PA - permanent uptime ults have to go - same with PL - the game needs an element of skill - most heroes have cooldown and this is a good thing - to priorities skillful timing and coordination. PL and PA should have similar ults - a window of opportunity. There you have it - my list of the heroes i can think of that really NEED to be fixed. You can always know a hero has a problem when it's high in popularity or has a high win rate as people don't pick heroes they will lose with no matter how much they enjoy. The heroes on this list have been a pain for me my ENTIRE 10000+ games. They have never fallen in line EVER they have just always been strong. Either they are just too strong or the rest of the roster is weak - or has a major weakness limiting them. There are so many heroes right now in the game that are balanced - these are the last few. Maybe in the future Witch Doctor and Riki but those aren't TOO bad they are just strong. The heroes on THIS LIST I have written are way too strong and need to be changed. Sadly, I am being reported because of this sound effect, and as a result, my conduct summary is being reduced. I believe this is a major issue faced by thousands of Dota 2 players all over the world. Since this is an ALL CHAT message, it means that both teams, including enemies, can hear it. Most of the time, people simply submit a random report against the player who owns this chat wheel sound, or any other chat wheel sound, or even for a harmless message such as “Good game, well played.” As a conclusion we got following main issues 1. Players are being unfairly reported for using officially purchased chat wheel sounds. 2. Conduct summary scores are being reduced due to reports unrelated to actual toxic behavior. 3. All-chat messages (including chat wheel sounds) are heard by both teams, increasing the chance of random or unjustified reports. 4. Even harmless or positive chat messages (e.g., “Good game, well played”) can trigger false reports. 5. This creates a negative experience for players who legally buy and use in-game content. I also want to share that I have many more ideas and suggestions on how to improve and fix certain aspects of the game, making both the player experience and the administrative work much easier. I would be more than happy if the Valve Support Team could contact me directly for a potential collaboration or partnership, in the name of keeping Dota 2 a safe, fair, and friendly place for everyone. Why deprive them of a microphone and chat in an eSports game where you need it because of some broken system that doesn't even work properly? Consider changing this integrity system. 60% of players have an integrity level below 8,000 and are unable to use voice chat. Lowering your integrity is easier than raising it, as your system deducts 1000 integrity for any misstep or report, and increases it by 300-350 for every 15 games played in Alpine Turbo—half the 150-230.
